title: Stance labels, written by a reader agent (prompts/stance.md) to <run>/stance/out-N.json; the merged rows in published/<run>/stances.jsonl and published/x/stances/<date>.jsonl are the same objects, one per line

key.description: the item's key from in-N.json, copied

labels.description: one per ticker the item is about, and one for each market target it takes a view on (@MARKET, @RATES, @CREDIT); a podcast claim needs one for each of its ticker candidates (a market target is optional); an X sentence or post may have none (no view, no label)

ticker.description: a US-listed ticker, or @MARKET (US stocks overall), @RATES (rates, the Fed, Treasuries), @CREDIT (spreads, high yield, private credit)

stance.description: -2 clearly bearish, -1 leaning bearish, 0 neutral or a mention, 1 leaning bullish, 2 clearly bullish

reason.description: under 15 words, in your own words

origin.description: optional, for a label with a stance other than 0: primary when the speaker is first-hand (an operator on their own business, a data source, giving their own view); recap when relaying news or someone else's view. The Alpha index (wire alpha-index) uses it; where it is missing a default rule decides.

horizon_days.description: optional, for a label with a stance other than 0: the trading days the view is about (5 a week, 21 a month, 63 a quarter), the nearest to what the speaker implies

target.description: optional: the company, or the sector or theme, the view is about, in words, when the ticker alone does not say it (an ETF, a market target, a supply-chain read)
